constraints: classification and refund eligibility are not the same responsibility
Seal and recall criteria are maintained separately; recall takes precedence when it applies, while refund eligibility remains independent.

feedback.reason: Seal evidence determines the ordinary result, but a safety recall takes precedence and refund eligibility remains separate. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: The returns workflow needs one classification result that honors recall precedence while leaving refunds to their own decision.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is let the caller select a reviewer from the return category before either reviewer checks the seal or recall facts. The category alone does not establish which reviewer can decide this item; choosing before eligibility bypasses the stated ordered checks. The contract instead requires one classification.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Separate ordered evaluation is useful while independent review rules can qualify from item facts and precedence matters. If a single authoritative code directly identifies one reviewer, direct dispatch is simpler.
details.transfer: For another return category, keep recall precedence in the classification result and do not absorb refund eligibility into it.

messages.text: The category alone does not establish which reviewer can decide this item; choosing before eligibility bypasses the stated ordered checks.
The prompt makes the ordered eligible result authoritative; reconciling both can replace that result with a competing class.
That makes every independently owned return rule a dispatcher change, even though the checks already have their own reviewers.
Arrival time can let the recall reviewer win before the earlier seal check has determined whether it applies.

options.text: Run classification handlers in order; each returns a class or passes, while refund eligibility stays separate.
Let the caller select a reviewer from the return category before either reviewer checks the seal or recall facts.
Let the seal reviewer and recall reviewer each return a class, then reconcile the two classifications afterward.
Add seal, recall, and future return-class branches to the warehouse dispatcher.
Run both reviews at once and use whichever classification arrives first.

prompt: In a returns inspection workflow, the warehouse inspector must classify a returned item. Seal condition determines the ordinary classification; a safety recall requires the unsafe classification to prevail. Refund eligibility is a separate decision, and assessment rules are maintained by separate reviewers. Which design keeps the classification outcome consistent as new assessment rules are added?

constraints: published outputs reference immutable inputs and code versions
Backend support varies by exact version pair, and configuration ranks the backends that support the requested pair.

feedback.reason: Publication must use the exact input/code pair and prefer the highest-ranked compatible backend. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A backend is usable only for the requested immutable pair, and configuration provides the winner when several backends are compatible.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is choose one snapshot backend from the experiment type before checking support for its input and code version. Experiment type does not prove backend support for this exact immutable pair; a preselected backend can reject when another ordered backend supports it. The contract instead requires one complete snapshot bound to that pair.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An ordered fallback is useful when support varies by exact version pair and configuration defines precedence. If each pair maps to one authoritative backend, direct lookup can replace fallback.
details.transfer: For another snapshot pair, preserve exact version matching and use the configured backend preference among compatible choices.

messages.text: Experiment type does not prove backend support for this exact immutable pair; a preselected backend can reject when another ordered backend supports it.
Partial compatibility with only one side of the pair is insufficient; combining fragments could bind output to incompatible versions.
The publication path would change whenever a backend is independently maintained, contrary to the separate-backend boundary.
Fast response is not the stated support or ordering criterion and can publish from a later backend.

options.text: Choose one snapshot backend from the experiment type before checking support for its input and code version.
Combine snapshot fragments from every backend that supports either the input or the code version.
Add each backend and its version rules to the notebook publication switch.
Ask all backends in parallel and publish the first response, even if an earlier configured backend supports the pair.
Try snapshot backends in order; return a complete version-bound snapshot or pass without publishing.

prompt: In a research-notebook platform, a snapshot must bind the exact immutable input and code-version pair it was produced from. Several independently maintained backends can support different pairs. When more than one backend supports the pair, notebook configuration ranks them and the highest-ranked compatible backend is preferred. Which design preserves that preference without changing publication code for each backend?

constraints: accepted comments must retain their author and document revision
The comment must retain its author and revision; destination preference and fallback apply to one notification.

feedback.reason: Author/revision attribution is part of the comment and exactly one configured notification destination should deliver the notice. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: The editor accepts one attributed comment; destination preference and fallback govern a single notification rather than multiple sends.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is let the assigned author choose a channel after acceptance without checking which channel handles that assignment. The scenario puts channel eligibility in the handlers; a recipient choice bypasses those independent channel rules. The contract instead requires one notice to the assigned author.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered fallback fits when one eligible channel should own delivery. If policy later requires all channels to receive a notice, model explicit fan-out and deduplication instead.
details.transfer: For a new notification destination, retain the comment ID and the one-notice rule while adding its preference explicitly.

messages.text: The scenario puts channel eligibility in the handlers; a recipient choice bypasses those independent channel rules.
The contract gives the first accepting channel ownership; sending to all channels risks duplicate notices and does not honor that ownership.
That couples comment acceptance to independently maintained channel rules and makes each channel change alter the editor.
The fastest receipt does not establish which channel accepts the assigned author; other sends may already have occurred.

options.text: Let the assigned author choose a channel after acceptance without checking which channel handles that assignment.
Send the comment to every configured channel and reconcile delivery receipts afterward.
Add each channel’s assignment rules to the comment-acceptance operation.
Offer the accepted comment to ordered notification handlers; stop when one accepts the assigned-author notice.
Notify all channels concurrently and keep whichever receipt arrives first.

prompt: In a collaborative annotation workspace, an accepted comment must retain its author and document revision. The assigned author has a preferred notification destination; if that destination is unavailable, an explicitly configured fallback is allowed. Only one notice may be sent for a comment. Which design handles destination eligibility without duplicating delivery?

constraints: a submission is either complete or explicitly retryable
The outcome is a complete inspection or retryable submission; local acceptance has priority over online acceptance.

feedback.reason: The whole inspection is accepted or remains retryable, and local acceptance has priority over online fallback. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A valid local submission should take precedence when it can store the complete payload; online is the fallback, not a partial second write.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is choose local queue or online submission from a connectivity flag before either handler examines the payload. Connectivity alone does not establish which handler can accept this offline payload; the prompt assigns that test to the handlers. The contract instead requires one complete submission outcome.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered fallback fits the local-first preference and full-record acceptance. If both destinations must receive the inspection, use an explicit replication workflow instead.
details.transfer: For another inspection payload, pass it to the preferred complete-acceptance path and use fallback only if that path cannot accept it.

messages.text: Connectivity alone does not establish which handler can accept this offline payload; the prompt assigns that test to the handlers.
The case explicitly forbids partial submission; combining section writes can create a record that is neither complete nor retryable.
Two accepted writes can duplicate one complete inspection instead of returning one complete or retryable outcome.
A faster partial or unsupported attempt could win; the contract asks each handler to accept the whole payload or pass.

options.text: Choose local queue or online submission from a connectivity flag before either handler examines the payload.
Upload any sections each handler accepts, then combine them into an inspection record.
Try submission handlers in order; one accepts the whole inspection or passes it unchanged for retry.
Let local and online handlers both accept the same inspection and reconcile their records later.
Race local queue and online submission, accepting whichever finishes first.

prompt: In a mobile field-inspection app, a submission is either a complete inspection or remains retryable; partial records are forbidden. Local storage is preferred when it can accept the full payload, with online submission as a fallback. Both paths use independently maintained acceptance rules. Which design preserves the preferred complete outcome?

constraints: the new issue is traceable and does not double-charge the customer
Reissue rules are maintained by their policy owners, and the replacement retains one traceable identity across retries.

feedback.reason: Overlapping rejection categories have an explicit policy priority, and the replacement must be traceable and non-duplicative. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: Only the highest-priority eligible rejection policy should issue the replacement, and retries must refer to that same replacement identity.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is have the caller map the rejection label to one handler before the handler checks its rejection-class coverage. A label-to-handler guess can bypass the stated coverage test; an ineligible handler must be able to pass. The contract instead requires one traceable replacement.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A priority-based chain fits overlapping policies maintained independently. If rejection codes are mutually exclusive and map authoritatively to one policy, direct dispatch is simpler.
details.transfer: For another rejection type, retain category priority and the one-replacement identity while adding its policy.

messages.text: A label-to-handler guess can bypass the stated coverage test; an ineligible handler must be able to pass.
More than one issue can charge the customer; reconciling afterward cannot undo the duplicate-charge risk in the stated workflow.
That makes class-specific reissue rules part of the shared service instead of independently owned handlers.
Response speed does not identify the eligible rejection-class owner and can start duplicate replacements.

options.text: Have the caller map the rejection label to one handler before the handler checks its rejection-class coverage.
Offer the rejected invoice to its ordered reissue handlers; the first eligible one issues its traceable replacement.
Ask every rejection-class handler to issue a replacement, then keep the most complete invoice.
Add every rejection class to one billing-service conditional and modify it for each new class.
Run all reissue handlers concurrently and accept the earliest replacement response.

prompt: In a digital invoice exchange, one rejected invoice may receive one traceable replacement without a second charge. Rejection categories can overlap, but finance defines a priority among their reissue policies; each policy owner maintains its rule independently. Which design selects the eligible reissue policy while preserving one replacement identity?

constraints: revocation is visible to the door policy before access is granted
Revocation has precedence over schedule-based permission; site-specific rules remain separately maintained.

feedback.reason: Revocation denial has precedence over schedule allowance and later rules cannot reverse it. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A door must not grant access through a schedule match after the badge’s revocation has already determined the outcome.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is check the schedule first and stop on its allow before looking for a badge revocation. That reverses the specified priority and can grant access to a revoked badge. The contract instead requires one terminal access decision.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered rules fit when a terminal safety decision outranks a later ordinary allowance. If the system needs every applicable denial reason for audit, collect those reasons separately from the access decision.
details.transfer: For another access rule, place it within the established precedence and keep revocation denial authoritative.

messages.text: That reverses the specified priority and can grant access to a revoked badge.
The prompt explicitly makes revocation terminal; aggregating allows would undo that stated denial.
Different callers could omit or reorder the required revocation-before-schedule sequence.
A schedule allow could arrive first and grant access before the revocation check finishes.

options.text: Evaluate the access rules in order; revocation is terminal, and an inapplicable rule passes.
Check the schedule first and stop on its allow before looking for a badge revocation.
Let any applicable schedule allow override a revocation denial after all rules have run.
Make each door caller choose whether to run revocation or schedule checks.
Run revocation and schedule rules concurrently and use whichever responds first.

prompt: In a smart-building access controller, a revoked badge must be denied before ordinary schedule access is considered. A later schedule allowance cannot override revocation. Site-specific access rules are added independently. Which design preserves that precedence?

constraints: the printed label represents the current approved shipment data
Formatter compatibility depends on the carrier/service pair, and configuration determines preference among compatible choices.

feedback.reason: The label must match the approved revision and the highest-ranked formatter supporting both carrier and service should own it. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A carrier-only match is insufficient; configured precedence chooses among formatters that support the requested pair.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is select a formatter from the carrier alone, then use its label even if it does not support the selected service. The prompt requires support for both carrier and service; a carrier-only match can produce an unsupported label. The contract instead requires one label for approved data.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An ordered fallback fits overlapping formatter capabilities and one-label ownership. If carrier/service resolves to one authoritative formatter, direct lookup is smaller.
details.transfer: For a new carrier/service pair, preserve approved-revision checking and add its formatter to the compatibility preference.

messages.text: The prompt requires support for both carrier and service; a carrier-only match can produce an unsupported label.
The contract assigns one label to the first formatter matching both facts; merged outputs can conflict on the approved shipment fields.
This leaks formatter capability details into callers that the scenario says should stay independent of format details.
A fast response is not evidence that the formatter supports both requested dimensions or the approved revision.

options.text: Select a formatter from the carrier alone, then use its label even if it does not support the selected service.
Merge carrier and service labels from every formatter into one final label.
Put carrier/service-specific format rules in the shipping caller and extend it for every formatter.
Ask every formatter concurrently and print the first label returned, regardless of its carrier/service support.
Try carrier/service label formatters in order; return the first label for approved shipment data.

prompt: In a package-label service, the label must reflect the current approved shipment revision. Carrier/service formatters support different combinations, and shipping configuration ranks the compatible formatters. Only one label should be printed. Which design selects a formatter without exposing format rules to callers?

constraints: the room capacity and cancellation policy must remain consistent
Room capacity and cancellation terms both constrain the move; priority applies when multiple rooms qualify.

feedback.reason: Both capacity and cancellation conditions must hold, and the first eligible room in configured preference owns the booking. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: Capacity alone cannot authorize a move; the destination must satisfy both checks before the one reservation transfer.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is choose the room with the most capacity before checking whether its cancellation terms permit this booking. Capacity alone is not sufficient; a larger room can fail the second stated eligibility check. The contract instead requires one qualifying destination room.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Priority-based fallback fits when multiple rooms may qualify but one should receive the booking. If the caller supplies one already-validated room, direct reservation is simpler.
details.transfer: For another booking, apply both destination checks before transferring the reservation and retain the configured room priority.

messages.text: Capacity alone is not sufficient; a larger room can fail the second stated eligibility check.
The prompt requires both checks before reservation; reserving on either can leave a booking in an ineligible room.
That makes the coordinator own the independently handled room checks instead of passing the request through them.
Response speed does not establish both eligibility conditions or the stated first-qualifying order.

options.text: Choose the room with the most capacity before checking whether its cancellation terms permit this booking.
Reserve every room that passes either capacity or cancellation, then choose one after all reservations complete.
Put every room’s eligibility conditions in the coordinator and update its switch for new room types.
Offer the room move to prioritized room handlers; the first that meets both conditions claims it.
Check all rooms concurrently and reserve whichever responds first.

prompt: In a multi-tenant rehearsal scheduler, a booking may move only to a room that has capacity and permits the cancellation policy. Eligible rooms have a configured priority; reserve only one destination. Which design finds the preferred valid room without splitting eligibility across callers?

constraints: unsafe commands are rejected while maintenance is active
Maintenance restrictions govern covered commands during maintenance mode; exhibit-specific restrictions are maintained independently.

feedback.reason: The maintenance restriction is a terminal rejection that unrelated allowances cannot override. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: The controller must treat the maintenance decision as authoritative before a command can execute; unrelated rules do not turn it into permission.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is treat the maintenance result as another pass so a later handler may execute the same unsafe command. Maintenance makes covered commands terminally invalid; passing that result would let later execution bypass the safety decision. The contract instead requires the first applicable safety outcome.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered terminal checks fit when one safety prohibition must dominate other rules. If the goal is only to collect explanatory warnings, evaluate them separately from execution permission.
details.transfer: For another exhibit command, preserve maintenance rejection precedence and keep unrelated safety findings from granting execution.

messages.text: Maintenance makes covered commands terminally invalid; passing that result would let later execution bypass the safety decision.
An allow aggregation can override the terminal invalid result required for covered unsafe commands.
Caller copies can omit or order the maintenance check differently, so the terminal safety boundary is no longer shared.
A later permissive response can arrive before the applicable maintenance rule returns its terminal invalid result.

options.text: Treat the maintenance result as another pass so a later handler may execute the same unsafe command.
Allow a command whenever any safety handler approves it, even if another applicable handler rejects it.
Pass the command through ordered safety handlers; the first applicable unsafe-command rule denies it.
Copy all safety predicates into each exhibit command caller.
Run safety checks concurrently and use the first response as the command outcome.

prompt: In a museum exhibit controller, commands covered by maintenance restrictions are invalid while maintenance mode is active. That rejection must prevail over any unrelated safety allowance. New exhibit-specific restrictions are maintained independently. Which design keeps a covered unsafe command from executing?

constraints: progress refers to a stable lesson identity
Progress formats differ, and the curriculum owner maintains migration support and a preferred format order.

feedback.reason: Retirement must retain progress under the same lesson identity and prefer supported migrations without partially retiring an unsupported record. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A supported progress representation can migrate under the stable lesson ID; an unsupported one cannot leave the lesson half-retired.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is have the caller choose a progress handler from the lesson category before checking which record form it supports. Lesson category does not establish record-form support; the selected handler must be allowed to pass when the form is unsupported. The contract instead requires one supported retirement operation.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered migration fallback fits when storage formats overlap and one supported migration should handle the record. If the record format identifies one migration directly, use that dispatch.
details.transfer: For another progress format, keep lesson identity stable and require the retirement outcome to remain retryable when no migration supports it.

messages.text: Lesson category does not establish record-form support; the selected handler must be allowed to pass when the form is unsupported.
Partial migration breaks the stated requirement to preserve learner progress for the stable lesson identity.
Each new stored form would change the retirement coordinator rather than its independently maintained handlers.
Combining unsupported or overlapping migrations risks duplicate or incompatible progress for the same lesson.

options.text: Have the caller choose a progress handler from the lesson category before checking which record form it supports.
Try progress handlers by supported record form; the first retires the lesson while preserving identity.
Retire the lesson as soon as any handler can migrate one record, then discard remaining progress records.
Add every progress-record format to a central retirement switch.
Run all progress handlers concurrently and combine the records they return.

prompt: In a video-learning library, retiring a lesson must preserve its stable identity and linked learner progress. Progress records use several formats; the curriculum owner maintains migration support in a declared format preference. An unsupported format must leave the lesson available for retry. Which design preserves this outcome?

constraints: export observes a stable session state
The host requests a signed audit format; exporter support varies by history format and configuration ranks compatible exporters.

feedback.reason: The request names the signed audit format, compatible exporters have precedence, and capture must precede close. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: The requested format and exporter preference select one complete bundle, while the pre-close capture preserves the session data it represents.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is close the board first and ask export handlers to read the live session afterward. The prompt says capture precedes close; reading after closure may no longer represent the captured session state. The contract instead requires one complete history export from the captured state.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered exporter fallback fits when support for the requested format varies and priority resolves multiple complete candidates. If one exporter is authoritative, direct dispatch is simpler.
details.transfer: For another export format, state its preference and continue exporting from the captured pre-close session state.

messages.text: The prompt says capture precedes close; reading after closure may no longer represent the captured session state.
Fragment combination does not guarantee one complete export of the already captured session state.
That couples independent export handlers to the close operation and changes it whenever a format is added.
The fastest live read is not the captured pre-close state the export must represent.

options.text: Try export handlers in order; return the first complete history for the stable session state.
Close the board first and ask export handlers to read the live session afterward.
Ask every exporter to serialize a fragment and combine the fragments after the board closes.
Make the board-closing operation contain a branch for every export format.
Run exporters against the live board concurrently and keep whichever finishes first.

prompt: In a shared whiteboard application, an export must represent the session state captured before the board closes. The host requests a signed audit bundle; compatible exporters have a configured preference order, and only a complete bundle is acceptable. Which design returns the preferred export from the captured state?

constraints: the escalation keeps ownership and response deadlines
Tier rules are maintained separately, and a missed response deadline disqualifies a tier from ownership.

feedback.reason: Tier priority and deadline eligibility together determine one owner for transfer and notice. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A tier that misses the deadline cannot claim the conversation; the selected eligible tier must be used consistently for ownership and notification.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is choose an escalation tier from the queue label before checking whether it can meet the response deadline. Queue label does not establish deadline eligibility; a tier that cannot meet the deadline must pass. The contract instead requires one eligible tier assignment.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An ordered eligibility check fits prioritized tiers with independent rules. If one stable case category always identifies its tier, direct routing is simpler.
details.transfer: For another support domain, preserve the response deadline and use one selected tier for both ownership transfer and notice.

messages.text: Queue label does not establish deadline eligibility; a tier that cannot meet the deadline must pass.
The prompt defines a selected eligible owner; multiple assignments and notices violate that outcome.
That turns independent tier rules into central routing changes whenever a tier is added or maintained.
Response speed can select an ineligible tier; the stated condition is ability to meet the deadline.

options.text: Choose an escalation tier from the queue label before checking whether it can meet the response deadline.
Assign every tier that might meet the deadline and reconcile ownership after notices are sent.
Put each tier’s deadline and coverage rules into the support desk dispatcher.
Ask all tiers in parallel and assign the first one to respond, even if it misses the deadline.
Offer escalation to ordered tiers; the first that can meet the deadline owns the conversation.

prompt: In a customer-support escalation desk, one tier should own a conversation: use the highest-priority tier that can meet the response deadline. Tier rules are maintained separately, and ownership transfer and notice must reflect the same selected tier. Which design selects a timely owner without duplicating tier policy in callers?

constraints: a listing cannot become visible before its price and stock rule are valid
Category rules are maintained separately; price and stock are both required for publication.

feedback.reason: Category precedence resolves overlap, and visibility requires both price and stock to be valid. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A category match does not by itself authorize publication; both required checks must pass before the listing is visible.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is publish when the matching category handler validates price, then check stock after the listing is visible. The prompt requires both price and stock validity before visibility; a later stock check is too late. The contract instead requires a visible listing after both checks pass.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Priority-based evaluation fits overlapping category rules with one publication outcome. If product category is unique and authoritative, direct rule lookup is simpler.
details.transfer: For another product category, keep visibility gated on both validations and retain the configured category priority.

messages.text: The prompt requires both price and stock validity before visibility; a later stock check is too late.
Pass means the handler does not own that category, not that another category may override a failed required validation.
That makes independently owned category rules central branches, so every category change alters publication code.
Approval of either one is insufficient and response timing cannot replace both required checks.

options.text: Publish when the matching category handler validates price, then check stock after the listing is visible.
Let the category handler pass after a failed price or stock check so another category handler can publish.
Add each category and its price/stock rules to the marketplace publication switch.
Pass the listing through ordered product rules; publish only after its matching rule validates price and stock.
Run category handlers concurrently and publish the first response that approves either price or stock.

prompt: In a regional produce marketplace, a listing may become visible only after its price and stock checks both pass. Product categories have a configured priority because some categories overlap, and each category owner maintains its own rule. Which design publishes only the eligible category’s listing?

constraints: each split retains the original request identity and delivery promise
Partial vendor fulfillment is allowed, but later offers apply only to the unfilled remainder.

feedback.reason: Partial vendor acceptance continues with the unfilled quantity under the same request identity and promise. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Each vendor receives only the still-unfilled quantity. A partial acceptance records that split and passes the remainder onward with the original request identity and delivery promise. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: The accepted portions accumulate, but no vendor receives units already accepted by a prior vendor; the final remainder remains visible.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is stop after the first vendor accepts any quantity and leave the rest outside the request. The contract explicitly passes the unfilled remainder onward; stopping loses the remaining quantity and promise. The contract instead requires accepted splits plus the final unfilled remainder.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered remainder handoff fits when vendors may fill portions in sequence. If allocation must optimize globally across all vendors or commit atomically, use a coordinator that computes that allocation.
details.transfer: For another vendor, carry forward only unfilled quantity and keep the original request identity and promise on every split.

messages.text: The contract explicitly passes the unfilled remainder onward; stopping loses the remaining quantity and promise.
That can allocate the same units more than once; later handlers must receive only the unfilled remainder.
Concurrent offers can commit overlapping quantities before reconciliation, unlike the ordered remainder handoff.
The prompt gives vendors their own acceptance decision; duplicating those rules centrally risks inconsistent allocations.

options.text: Stop after the first vendor accepts any quantity and leave the rest outside the request.
Send the original full quantity to each later vendor after a partial acceptance.
Offer each vendor the remaining quantity; accept a split or pass the remainder while retaining request identity.
Start all vendor offers concurrently and reconcile their quantities after replies arrive.
Have the dispatcher own each vendor’s stock rules and calculate every split itself.

prompt: In a repair-parts marketplace, a backordered request may be split across vendors. Each accepted portion reduces the remaining quantity; later vendors receive only that remainder. All splits must retain the original request identity and delivery promise, and vendor priority is configured. Which design preserves those facts through partial fulfillment?

constraints: transfer preserves the plot boundary and approval history
Boundary coverage determines authority, with specificity resolving overlap; approval history remains attached to the reservation.

feedback.reason: Boundary coverage and specificity determine one approve/deny decision while approval history remains attached. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: An authority outside the plot boundary cannot decide; among covering authorities, the most specific one is authoritative.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is accept the first authority response even when that authority does not cover this plot boundary. An uncovered authority must pass; accepting its result gives a decision to the wrong boundary owner. The contract instead requires one applicable approval or denial with history.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An ordered authority check fits overlapping boundary scopes with a specificity rule. If every boundary maps to one unique authority, direct lookup is simpler.
details.transfer: For another plot, retain the boundary-specific approval history and apply specificity before accepting a transfer decision.

messages.text: An uncovered authority must pass; accepting its result gives a decision to the wrong boundary owner.
The prompt assigns one covered authority to decide; requiring unrelated authorities changes that approval contract.
A plot name alone may select an authority that does not cover its boundary, duplicating eligibility logic in callers.
Fastest response does not establish boundary coverage and can select an unrelated authority.

options.text: Accept the first authority response even when that authority does not cover this plot boundary.
Evaluate transfer authorities in order; the first applicable decision approves or denies without losing history.
Require every authority in the list to approve before any reservation can transfer.
Let each calling screen choose an authority from the plot name without applying coverage checks.
Run all authorities concurrently and keep whichever approve/deny response arrives first.

prompt: In a community garden allocation tool, only an authority covering a plot boundary may decide its reservation transfer. Where authorities overlap, the most specific boundary has precedence. The transfer must retain its approval history. Which design reaches the applicable authority without duplicating boundary checks across screens?

constraints: the bundle pricing policy remains consistent with its components
Regional rules are maintained separately, and component pricing inputs may change after the bundle is created.

feedback.reason: Region precedence chooses one rule and that rule must use the bundle’s current component prices. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A result from a lower-priority or nonmatching region is not the bundle price; the calculation must use current component inputs.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is use the bundle price cached when it was first created, regardless of current component pricing inputs. The prompt requires the matching region handler to compute from current component inputs, so a stale cached price can violate that basis. The contract instead requires one bundle price based on current component inputs.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered policy evaluation fits overlapping regional rules where configuration defines preference. If a bundle carries one definitive region key, direct lookup may be enough.
details.transfer: For another regional bundle, preserve the configured region preference and calculate from current component inputs.

messages.text: The prompt requires the matching region handler to compute from current component inputs, so a stale cached price can violate that basis.
Different regions are alternatives, not additive components; combining their returns mixes incompatible regional calculations.
That centralizes rules the scenario assigns to regional handlers and requires dispatcher edits for each region.
Response time does not establish that the handler matches the bundle region.

options.text: Try regional pricing handlers in order; the matching handler computes from the bundle’s component inputs.
Use the bundle price cached when it was first created, regardless of current component pricing inputs.
Combine prices returned by every regional handler into one bundle price.
Put regional formulas in one bundle-creation switch and add each region there.
Ask regional handlers concurrently and use the first price returned without checking its region.

prompt: In a subscription packaging service, regional pricing rules may overlap, and catalog configuration ranks regions for a bundle. The selected region must calculate from current component pricing inputs, not a stale bundle total. Which design resolves the regional rule while preserving that calculation basis?

constraints: charger capacity and reservation expiry are coordinated
Capacity and expiry are separate conditions on a claim; a slot must satisfy both.

feedback.reason: Station priority selects one claimant, but capacity and expiry must both permit the requested time. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: A station with capacity but an incompatible expiry is not eligible; the coordinator must select one valid claim in priority order.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is claim the first slot with capacity, then check whether its reservation expiry permits the requested time. Capacity alone is insufficient; the claim must satisfy both facts before reserving. The contract instead requires one eligible station claim.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Ordered fallback fits prioritized stations with per-slot eligibility. If a solver must optimize a slot across all stations globally, calculate the candidate set before one claim.
details.transfer: For another charger slot, keep both capacity and expiry in the eligibility check before accepting the prioritized claim.

messages.text: Capacity alone is insufficient; the claim must satisfy both facts before reserving.
Multiple claims can exist before cancellation and may conflict; the case requires a priority-ordered eligible claim.
This duplicates station eligibility and can bypass the required priority order across handlers.
Arrival order can bypass station priority or select a response that has not passed the expiry check.

options.text: Claim the first slot with capacity, then check whether its reservation expiry permits the requested time.
Reserve the slot at every station that reports capacity and cancel all but one afterward.
Let the operator choose a station from its name and perform capacity/expiry checks in the caller.
Ask stations concurrently and keep the first response, even when an earlier-priority station is eligible.
Offer the slot to station handlers in priority order; the first with capacity and a valid expiry claims it.

prompt: In a fleet charging coordinator, one station should claim a requested slot according to station priority. A claim is valid only if both charger capacity and reservation expiry permit that slot. Which design avoids a duplicate or expired claim?

constraints: asset identity remains stable while descriptive values are replaced
Conflict rules may overlap, but only a rule that recognizes the conflict may alter descriptive metadata.

feedback.reason: One prioritized rule resolves each recognized conflict, while a nonmatching rule cannot mutate either source record. The design must realize this outcome while leaving rule-specific behavior independently maintained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An applicable handler returns its result and ends evaluation; a handler whose stated qualification does not apply passes so the next ordered handler can inspect the request. This separates sequencing from each handler’s case-specific eligibility rule.
details.scenarioApplication: Metadata changes are scoped to a recognized conflict and do not create a new asset identity or let a nonowner edit records.
details.errorCorrection: The closest wrong approach is let every metadata handler apply its changes even when it does not recognize the conflict, then roll back if needed. The prompt requires non-owning handlers to pass without changing either record; later rollback is not that pass contract. The contract instead requires one recognized conflict resolution without changing asset identity.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An ordered conflict-resolution path fits overlapping rules with a defined priority. If conflicts are mutually exclusive and have one authoritative resolver, direct dispatch is simpler.
details.transfer: For another metadata conflict, retain asset identity and require only the prioritized recognizing rule to change the records.

messages.text: The prompt requires non-owning handlers to pass without changing either record; later rollback is not that pass contract.
That bypasses conflict ownership and may combine incompatible changes across the two source records.
The case explicitly keeps asset identity stable while descriptive values are replaced.
A concurrent mutation can come from a handler that does not own the conflict and may alter a record before ownership is known.

options.text: Let every metadata handler apply its changes even when it does not recognize the conflict, then roll back if needed.
Merge each field in the caller by asking all handlers for a preferred value.
Create a new asset identity for each resolved metadata conflict.
Offer each conflict to its metadata handler; the first matching handler resolves it without changing asset identity.
Run every conflict handler at once and retain the first mutation observed.

prompt: In a photo-archive curation tool, asset identity must remain stable while descriptive metadata is merged. Conflict rules may overlap, but only the highest-priority rule that recognizes a conflict may change the records; a nonmatching rule must leave both unchanged. Which design preserves conflict ownership?
